From the owner
Every opening in the wall is a problem to solve. Cut a hole for a window or a door and you’ve removed the studs that were carrying everything above them. The header is what picks that load back up and walks it out to the king and jack studs on either side. Swipe 2 — that’s a load-bearing header. Laminated veneer lumber, carrying the second floor and the roof above it. Sized by span and load, not by habit. Swipe 3 — a non-bearing opening. Nothing stacked above it, so the header is framing the opening, not fighting gravity. From the finished side, you’ll never tell them apart. That’s the point. The difference shows up in year ten, in whether the drywall above your door stays straight. Framing is the part nobody sees and everybody lives in.
